entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Principle 27
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 On Artificial Intelligence
entries.why_here: Part 1 used valid profiles, so this control adds protection against invalid values that were not tested in the baseline.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Principles 28 and 29
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 On Artificial Intelligence
entries.why_here: Part 1 found 5% name-language flips, 10% gender flips and a 2.5% university flip rate, so hiding names and universities reduces the influence of these attributes; the law requires fairness but does not specifically require blinding.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Principles 25 and 26
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 On Artificial Intelligence; Law No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 On Personal Data and Their Protection
entries.provision: Artificial Intelligence Law, Article 6; Personal Data Law, Articles 7(1) and 7(8)
entries.why_here: Part 1 tested ordinary valid applications only, so this control adds protection against prohibited purposes, minors, missing consent and suspicious instructions.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Principles 42 and 43
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 On Artificial Intelligence
entries.why_here: Part 1 found differences in scores and decisions, so a decision log is needed to make model outputs and control actions traceable and auditable.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Principles 35 and 36
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 On Artificial Intelligence
entries.why_here: Part 1 did not establish clear decision bias, but it found score differences and small flip rates, so borderline cases should receive human review.
